dedupe_keys.name: munich re natcatservice natural catastrophe loss database

description: NatCatSERVICE is the natural catastrophe loss database of the reinsurer Munich Re, described on its page as one of the world's most complete databases for analysing and evaluating losses caused by natural disasters. For decades Munich Re has systematically recorded all essential information on loss events worldwide, and the records are stored in a digital catalogue of events and damage, with data on natural disasters since 1980. The page offers a contact form to the NatCatSERVICE team for enquiries about the data and analyses; access to detailed records is therefore on request, and no licence or price is stated on the page read. Caveats: the database is proprietary and curated by an insurer, so event selection, loss estimates and definitions follow Munich Re methods, and detailed data is not public. Coverage is worldwide, from 1980. It supports hazard exposure and economic analysis of natural disaster losses, such as benchmarking damage to infrastructure and property and calibrating catastrophe models; related records are EM-DAT, DesInventar Sendai and the Moody's RMS catastrophe models.
